title: Show HN: Today's cities on a globe of Earth's tectonic past and future
text:
Rotate
Add
Time
Today
Modern Earth
0 Ma
Today's countries and cities are used as colored crust markers. Country polygons are split by the
 present-day static polygons from the Merdith 2021 plate model, then each country-on-plate fragment is
 reconstructed backward with pyGPlates finite rotations. The future side is a constant-motion
 extrapolation from young plate rotations with a few coarse collision handoffs, so treat it as an
 interactive sketch rather than a forecast. Red areas mark plate fragments that still overlap after
 reconstruction.

comment.text:
Very nicely done. Plate coloring helped, as did the red highlights for plates pressuring each other.

New for me: I didn't realize eastern russia was at the north pole 220 Mya, and rotated and came south; at the same time, no real China, and India was at the South pole. America's, Africa, Australia didn't change much, but huge changes elsewhere.
Alas, no Singapore.  I wonder if you can add more cities?
there's actually a little [+] button that allows you to add one city

This is really cool!

I'm wondering what data you're using and if you can impose a more precise coordinate system into the visualizations with ways to track a specific point (perhaps starting from polygons or GPS coordinates). It seems the visualization includes sea level rise but it's hard to figure out if its getting other details right like the California’s Transverse Ranges uplift (~20 mYa to present) which moved the Los Angeles basin several hundred kilometers northwest all while San Diego and Baja California were also rearranged.
Is the triangle ‘play’ button supposed to do something? Maybe hug of death going on?
It feels like I might need 130 million years to watch the whole thing play out
